brief:
Dubai has set a date for one of the largest Palestinian cultural gatherings the UAE has hosted: the "Emirates Loves Palestine" festival fills South Halls 1 and 2 of the Dubai Exhibition Centre at Expo City Dubai on Saturday, August 29, the Khaleej Times reported. The celebration runs twelve hours, from noon to midnight, and entry is free for visitors who register in advance.

The organisers promise a full day built around three strands of Palestinian life: heritage displays, traditional cuisine, and performances by folk singers and other artists. The format is a family day as much as a concert — food vendors, artisans and community groups sharing two exhibition halls with the stage.

> Twelve hours, two halls, free entry — one day of Palestine at Expo City.

![Emirates Loves Palestine: the day at a glance](times-of-palestine-emirates-loves-palestine-details-2026.svg)

## A platform that has already filled these halls

The day comes from Emirates Loves, a community platform in the UAE that builds social-media channels — and now large public celebrations — around the success stories of the country's communities. Its Palestine channel, «الإمارات تحب فلسطين», highlights what Palestinians are building in the Emirates, in Palestine and around the world, and the festival carries that same name onto a physical stage.

The format arrives proven. The platform's Pakistan edition drew more than 60,000 people to the same venue for Pakistan's independence day earlier this month, Gulf News reported, with Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, the UAE minister of tolerance and coexistence, joining the crowds — a scale that turned a community celebration into one of Dubai's flagship public events.

## A stage the community rarely gets at this size

For the Palestinian community in the Emirates, the significance is the scale itself. Palestinian culture in the diaspora usually travels through small rooms — a film screening, a restaurant, an embroidery workshop — and August 29 offers instead the kind of national-scale venue that Expo City reserves for its biggest community days.

It is also a working marketplace for Palestinian culture at a moment when its home ground is under siege: the cooks, performers and artisans who fill the halls get a paying audience of thousands, and a generation of children raised in the Gulf gets a day inside the food, music and embroidery their parents carried with them. That is cultural support in the most practical currency — attendance.

## If you plan to go

The festival runs from 12pm to midnight on Saturday, August 29, in South Halls 1 and 2 of the Dubai Exhibition Centre at Expo City Dubai, which sits on the Route 2020 metro line. Entry is free, but the organisers require advance registration through their site, emiratesloves.com.

The performer line-up had not been published when this report was filed; the organisers' channels are releasing programme details in the run-up to the day. Times of Palestine will cover the festival itself in both languages.
